Dave Brubeck was born in Concord, California on December 6, 1920. His original work ranges from solo piano compositions to oratorios for choir and symphony orchestra. He continues to be a positive force around the world as a performer, educator, composer and humanitarian.
Dave was interviewed at his home in Wilton, Connecticut on November 21, 2001, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.
My name is Monk Rowe and I’m very privileged to be speaking with Dave Brubeck today in his home in Wilton, Connecticut. Thank you for taking time out of your day with me.

That’s true — I wonder if that was subliminal. It’s a real pleasure to be here and look around your room and all the history, and you go back so far. And I really feel a need to congratulate you on this career that is ongoing and very important in American music.

Yeah. I’m busier now than I ever was, and ever expected to be. Because every day it seems to get worse, demands, and to finish stuff. And these rooms are full of unfinished projects that I’d like to do.
I recently read a little article that I think came from — you were in San Diego, recently, weren’t you?
And someone quoted you as saying if you could finish all the work you had you’d be very happy.
